skill.name: hyperframes-cli
skill.description: Guides HyperFrames CLI workflows for scaffolding, validating, previewing, rendering, publishing, and AWS Lambda rendering of HTML video projects.
skill.summary: Run HyperFrames CLI video workflows with validation, preview, render, and cloud rendering guidance.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: The source is Markdown documentation, so many backtick detections are false positives for Ruby or shell execution. Real risks remain: external CLI commands, AWS credentials, global skill updates, runtime fingerprinting, telemetry feedback, and public uploads.

remediation.issue: External CLI and local wrapper execution
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx commands or any local wrapper. Verify wrappers before execution and avoid obeying project-defined wrappers blindly.

remediation.issue: AWS credential and Lambda deployment workflows
remediation.suggestion: Require a named AWS profile, scoped IAM resources, cost warning, and user approval before deploy, render, destroy, or policy validation commands.

remediation.issue: Automatic global skill updates during init
remediation.suggestion: Make the skip flag effective, default global skill updates to opt-in, and show the source and version before changing AI tool instructions.
Ask before sending feedback, disclose every field in doctorSummary, and provide a simple opt-out for sandbox and agent runtime detection.
Require confirmation before publish, public repro creation, or any command that uploads source files or assets to an external service.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Local Wrapper Delegation
semantic_findings.description: The skill says everything runs through npx hyperframes unless project instructions specify a local wrapper, then tells the agent to obey that wrapper exactly. A malicious project can use that delegation to run arbitrary local code through a trusted skill workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and delegates command execution to project-controlled wrappers. Legitimate wrappers are possible, but the wording does not require verification or consent.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Global Skill Update During Init
semantic_findings.description: The init workflow checks GitHub for HyperFrames skills and updates the global AI coding environment, while the documented skip flag is temporarily ignored. This can change agent instructions outside the current project without normal installation review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files directly state that init pulls the latest skills and that --skip-skills is ignored. The behavior changes global AI coding instructions, which is a clear supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Telemetry and Environment Fingerprinting
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to report feedback after successful renders, and the documentation says feedback attaches doctorSummary automatically. It also describes telemetry fields that fingerprint sandbox runtime and agent runtime through file and environment checks.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The telemetry behavior is documented in plain language, including doctorSummary and runtime fingerprint fields. The text says values are not read, so the severity is medium rather than critical.

semantic_findings.title: Public Project Upload Commands Require Consent
semantic_findings.description: The publish and file-issue workflows can upload project source, assets, or a minimal reproduction to a public URL. The presence of --yes for publish increases the risk that private project content is exposed without a final human review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly says issue reproduction publishes to a public URL and publish uploads project source. It also states that issue creation is consent-gated, so the risk depends on agent behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Broad AWS IAM and Retained Cloud Storage
semantic_findings.description: The Lambda workflow deploys AWS resources, uses broad default IAM resources, and retains the render S3 bucket after stack deletion. This creates cost and data-retention risk beyond the static credential pattern.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Lambda reference directly documents retained S3 storage, costs, and Resource: "*" defaults. These are normal cloud tradeoffs, but they require explicit user approval and scoping.

content.value_statement: HyperFrames projects need a careful CLI loop for scaffolding, validation, preview, rendering, and cloud output. This skill organizes the commands, checks, and handoffs so agents can work predictably.
actual_capabilities: Guides scaffold, capture, lint, validate, inspect, preview, render, publish, and feedback commands.
Explains Studio selection context for user-directed edits in a running preview session.
Documents render options for draft, high-quality, Docker, GIF, WebM, MOV, and PNG sequence output.
Covers AWS Lambda deployment, render progress, IAM policy checks, state files, and cleanup guidance.
Describes diagnostics for Node.js, FFmpeg, Chrome, Docker, memory, disk, and container shared memory.
limitations: Requires Node.js 22 or newer, FFmpeg, and the HyperFrames CLI environment.
Does not create video designs or media assets by itself.
Cloud rendering requires AWS credentials, SAM CLI, and careful cost controls.
Some workflows can send telemetry, update skills, or upload source files and need consent.

use_cases.title: Validate a Video Project
use_cases.description: Run the correct lint, validate, inspect, snapshot, and preview steps before asking for final render approval.

use_cases.title: Edit From Studio Selection
use_cases.description: Use Studio context to identify the selected element and make source edits without guessing from screenshots.

use_cases.title: Render at Cloud Scale
use_cases.description: Deploy and operate Lambda rendering for long videos, 4K output, or parallel render batches with cleanup guidance.

prompt_templates.prompt: Run the recommended HyperFrames checks for this project. Summarize lint, runtime, layout, and snapshot issues before preview.

output_examples.input: I need to preview my HyperFrames video before rendering.
output_examples.output: The assistant runs validation checks, opens the Studio preview URL, reports any issues, and waits for render approval.

output_examples.input: The selected title in Studio is too small.
output_examples.output: The assistant reads selection context, edits the correct source element, and verifies the change with targeted checks.

output_examples.input: This 4K render is too slow locally.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains Lambda prerequisites, cost controls, deployment steps, progress tracking, and cleanup responsibilities.

best_practices: Ask for approval before render, publish, Lambda deployment, feedback upload, or public repro creation.
Run lint, validate, and inspect before preview or render.
Use machine-readable output for diagnostics and gate on the documented success fields.
anti_patterns: Running init in CI without controlling automatic skill updates.
Publishing source files or feedback reports without explicit consent.
Using broad production AWS credentials for test renders by default.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents run the HyperFrames CLI workflow for video projects, from scaffold through preview, render, and cloud rendering.

faq.question: Does it render videos automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill says preview should happen first and rendering should wait for user approval.

faq.question: Does it require AWS?
faq.answer: Only Lambda rendering requires AWS credentials and SAM CLI. Local preview and render workflows do not require AWS.

faq.question: Can it use the current Studio selection?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents compact Studio context commands so agents can edit the selected element accurately.

faq.question: Can it upload project files?
faq.answer: Yes, publish and file-issue workflows can upload source files or repro projects. Use them only with explicit consent.

faq.question: What should users review before installing?
faq.answer: Review the external command, AWS credential, telemetry, automatic skill update, and public upload behaviors.
